With 126 of 127 issues attributed to Facilities/Site Management, this is a single-owner problem with a clear operational fix. A structured inspection regime with named accountability is the highest-leverage intervention available.

actions.action: Commission a capital refresh of waiting area furniture and amenities at the five highest-complaint dealerships (VIC06, QLD02, VIC03, QLD08, VIC02) within the next six months. Minimum scope per site: replace broken or torn seating with ergonomic chairs (comments reference hard chairs, low chairs, and torn vinyl); install a minimum of four power points and reliable Wi-Fi with a posted password in each lounge; service or replace non-functioning coffee machines (do not retain a machine that cannot be maintained — replace with a quality pod machine on a service contract); add a dedicated children's area with at minimum a mat, a small table, and two or three activity items; install at least one baby change table in each customer toilet. Simultaneously mandate accessible parking signage and disability-compliant drop-off at all sites, with VIC06 and QLD02 prioritised given volume. Parking layout review (staff vs. customer bays, pothole repair, line remarking) to be completed as part of the same site visit.
actions.owner: Facilities/Site Management (capital works) — State General Managers to approve budgets; individual Dealer Principals to scope and project-manage local works with a central Facilities coordinator
actions.measure: Waiting area comfort sub-theme complaints (currently 28) to fall by at least 60% within three quarters of completion; parking complaints (currently 24) to halve within one quarter of remediation works; post-visit CSI scores for 'dealership facilities' to improve by a minimum of 0.5 points on a 5-point scale at the five target sites; Wi-Fi and power point availability complaints to reach zero within one quarter of installation
actions.rationale: Waiting area comfort (28 issues) and parking (24 issues) together represent 41% of sub-theme complaints and require physical investment rather than process change alone. Customer comments describe worn carpet, scuffed walls, dead pot plants, torn vinyl, freezing lounges with no heating, no power points, dropping Wi-Fi, and car parks with potholes and no clear markings — all indicators of accumulated underinvestment rather than one-off incidents. Multiple customers explicitly note the mismatch between premium vehicle price points ($60k+) and the standard of facilities, which creates a brand credibility risk beyond mere inconvenience. The five priority sites are identifiable and manageable. Note: the data does not tell us current capital budgets or lease constraints at these sites, so the hypothesis is that budget approval is the primary barrier — this should be validated with Dealer Principals before scoping.

actions.action: Develop and install a clear, consistent wayfinding and signage system across all service-department sites, with particular urgency at multi-entrance facilities. Minimum requirements: external signage at every vehicle entry point directing service customers to the correct bay (with 'Service Customers' and an arrow — not just a brand logo); dedicated customer parking bays marked and enforced (staff vehicles must not occupy customer bays — Dealer Principals to issue a standing instruction to staff); a covered or at minimum clearly signed walkway from customer parking to service reception; internal signage directing customers to the waiting lounge and toilets without requiring them to pass through the workshop floor. At sites where toilet access currently requires walking through the workshop (at least one comment describes a near-slip incident), install a compliant internal route or a separate access point as a safety priority.
actions.owner: Facilities/Site Management for physical works; Dealer Principal at each site for staff parking enforcement policy; State OH&S coordinator to assess the workshop-access toilet safety issue
actions.measure: Parking and wayfinding complaints (currently embedded across the 24 parking issues and multiple comments referencing confusion at entry) to fall by at least 40% within two quarters; zero repeat incidents of customers entering the workshop to access toilets (OH&S log); customer satisfaction question relating to 'ease of arrival and navigation' (if not currently tracked, add to post-visit survey within one quarter)
actions.rationale: Multiple comments describe customers walking around buildings in heat, parking on the street and carrying children and equipment, being directed by staff to already-full bays, and nearly slipping on a wet workshop floor when trying to reach a toilet. These are both experience failures and safety risks. The wayfinding issue disproportionately affects first-time visitors and customers who are new to the area — a segment mentioned frequently in the sample comments — making it a retention risk as well as a satisfaction one. This is ranked third because the financial and reputational impact is somewhat lower than cleanliness (which affects every visit) and comfort investment (which has a direct brand-perception effect), but the OH&S dimension of the workshop-access toilet issue means it should not be deprioritised indefinitely.
